cua_changes_since_20261006.summary: Unchanged between 4f33cd6 and c1c2b5f: the native macOS ledger, the shared web ledger, the browser support table, the canvas/Qt/OpenGL rule and the Catalyst/Electron text-input limits. The declared support per framework is therefore the same as on 6 Oct.

Adds a launch_app urls row, the 250-node get_window_state cap with since diffs and tree_format, since:latest with include_screenshot:false, collapsed menus in reads, and invoke_menu in the Finder example. No change to any framework statement.

New efficient loop: targeted query reads, run_actions with observe:true as the default way to act, and foreground_fallback for steps refused because the app ignores background input (Electron, LibreOffice).

Documents that on Electron/Chromium windows a background scroll now reveals content through AX instead of posting wheel events, with foreground as fallback. This contradicts the unchanged ledger row that lists Electron scroll as background_unavailable.
Scroll Electron/Chromium windows in the background through AXScrollToVisible; nothing posted or fronted.

Same-pid keyboard ambiguity check ignores off-screen or zero-size sibling windows and every sibling when AX proves the target is the app's key window; typed newline and tab become real Return and Tab keys. May change the Safari two-window refusal seen on 6 Oct only when the second window is hidden or the target is the key window.
cua_changes_since_20261006.note: Needs a live check; not verified here.

cua_changes_since_20261006.summary: Background type_text with a line break into a Chromium native field (omnibox) is refused with browser_field_needs_keystrokes; foreground typing into browsers now fully activates the window, waits 250 ms and restores the field focus.
Background right click is posted once instead of twice on macOS.
LibreOffice and Tk-style pointer-reading toolkits refuse background pixel clicks; run_actions gains foreground_fallback. No listed benchmark framework is affected directly.
Menu-bar item tokens run as invoke_menu inside run_actions.

get_window_state is slimmed (250-node cap, one tree form, menus collapsed, metadata dropped) and batching is the default path, so the 6 Oct Cua full-read token and byte figures no longer describe the c1c2b5f binary.
No doc or code change found that adds or removes declared support for Catalyst, OpenGL/GLFW, Qt or Adobe.

claims_not_found.item: Any statement naming Photoshop, Adobe or UXP in libs/cua-driver docs, skills or the docs site (only unrelated blog and sample files match).
A Mac Catalyst row in the accepted native macOS ledger; only the text-input limits and a Proposed plan row (source-supported candidate, runtime row required).
kitty or GLFW by name; OpenGL viewports are named in the canvas rule, so the foreground-only claims are inferred.
Qt in the accepted ledger (absent); the only Qt statements are the canvas rule and a Proposed plan row.
Obsidian, Stocks, Calculator, TextEdit, Chrome and Safari by name; claims are framework-level (shared Electron host, AppKit, SwiftUI and WKWebView fixtures, Catalyst text-input limits).
Native press key and hotkey for AppKit, SwiftUI, and scroll for SwiftUI: the ledger lists them as unproven gaps, neither supported nor refused.
A Chromium row in the native ledger; Chromium claims come from MACOS.md, BROWSER.md and platform-support.mdx.
Mac Catalyst, Stocks, OpenGL, GLFW, kitty and Obsidian in any Driver guide, ADR or report (kitty appears only as a Stage Manager thumbnail in the T13 campaign).
SwiftUI as a named framework: Calculator is documented as native or AppKit, and LaunchCompatibility lists only AppKit, Chromium, Electron and Qt.
WebKit in LaunchCompatibility's supported list; Safari evidence is workflow-specific (field replace and button click).
